page: Amazon Web Services g4ad.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance featuring an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor with 8 vCPUs and 4 physical cores running at 3.0 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Graphics acceleration is delivered via a single AMD Radeon Pro Navi V520 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 300 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average performance across several standard workloads, though CPU-bound tasks show some limitations. The instance achieves average scores in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, as well as in ray tracing, image processing, and software compilation. However, stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10%, and multi-core performance is in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is also weak, falling in the bottom 25% for both read and write operations, whereas small block cached reads perform in the middle 50%.

The g4ad.2xlarge offers a balanced resource profile for graphics-intensive applications that benefit from AMD GPU acceleration and local NVMe storage, such as game streaming, remote workstations, and basic image processing. However, the weak multi-threaded decompression and poor raw CPU stress performance make it less suitable for heavy compute-bound or large-scale LLM inference tasks, where 7B model inference speeds drop to weak or poor levels. It represents a specialized hardware profile where cost efficiency is driven by the integration of a budget-friendly AMD GPU and local NVMe storage rather than raw CPU compute power.
description: Amazon Web Services g4ad.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for graphics-intensive workloads. It features an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor with 8 vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory. The instance includes a dedicated AMD Radeon Pro Navi V520 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM and a 300 GB NVMe SSD local instance store. Performance benchmarks show average results for Geekbench ray tracing, image processing, and software compilation, though raw CPU stress-ng performance is weak to poor. Large-block memory bandwidth is also limited, falling in the bottom 25%. This instance is suited for remote workstations, game streaming, and moderate graphics processing where local NVMe storage and AMD GPU acceleration are required, but it is less optimal for heavy compute-bound tasks or large language model inference.
